_meta.notes: Kerbostationary orbit, period exactly 1 Kerbin day (6 hours = 21600 s). Dot should land exactly on the Kepler curve at the synchronous crossing. 2863.33 km is the commonly-cited kerbosynchronous ALTITUDE, not SMA (radius from centre); the vessel.orbit emit's sma is altitude + Kerbin's 600 km radius, solved backward from T=2*pi*sqrt(sma^3/mu) at mu=3531600000000 so the dot lands exactly on this fixture's own reference curve: sma=3468751 (o.sma/o.period are unread legacy mirrors kept close to the commonly-cited numbers; the emit was left at the same 700000 boilerplate as every other Navball/EscapeProfile fixture, which put the dot in the low-sma corner regardless of scenario).
